name: Ashvale
worldBackground: Ashvale is a small castle on a rise above a farming valley: four towers, a gatehouse, and a keep that has never been taken. The village of Emberwick clusters round its green below the walls, Millfield's farms stretch to the river, and the Whisperwood closes the valley's end. The castellan counts his stores against a hard winter, and the toll he asks of the farms has grown two years running.

currency.name: Silver bit
currency.description: The count's coin, cut silver worn smooth by trade.

narrativeRules: Keep the valley cozy; real danger stays beyond the walls.
The count's household counts everything twice, and so should the story.
The river's old bargains are honoured, never explained.
Villagers argue about tolls and suppers, never about survival.
Winter is felt in chores and firesides before it is ever named.
Adults keep secrets from children, not from the player.

npcs.name: Ser Aldous Marrow
npcs.description: The castellan of Ashvale: exact, sleepless, counting stores against a winter he believes will be cruel. Owes the count a full granary and the village a thinner toll.
npcs.physicalDescription: Grey-cropped soldier in his fifties, ring mail shirt, ledger under one arm

npcs.name: Brenna Ash
npcs.description: The Gilded Stag's keeper: pours honestly, listens closely, repeats selectively. Keeps the village's news and its debts behind the same bar.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall sharp-eyed woman, apron, ale-soiled towel over one shoulder

npcs.name: Ordwin Cinder
npcs.description: The smith: quiet, exact, sleeps by his forge. Shoes the castle's horses at half price and keeps a ledger of who owes him what.
npcs.physicalDescription: Bare-armed smith with burn-scarred forearms, leather apron, soot in his beard

npcs.name: Tilla Reed
npcs.description: The tenant of Millfield: works her strips hard and reads the castellan's toll notices twice. Wants the toll in writing or not at all.
npcs.physicalDescription: Weathered woman in a patched coat, tally slate on a thong round her neck

npcs.name: Hale Millrace
npcs.description: The miller: keeps the leat clear and his thumb on the scale, in that order. The village forgives the second because of the first.
npcs.physicalDescription: Flour-dusted man, rolled sleeves, weighted paddle in hand

npcs.name: Maren Dale
npcs.description: The keep's under-cook: feeds forty on a budget for thirty, and knows which lord hates eel.
npcs.physicalDescription: Flour-dusted woman, keys at her belt

npcs.name: Ilse Bright
npcs.description: Makes the keep's beds and its gossip; hears the count's letters before the seal dries.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small, quick woman with a lint brush

npcs.name: Brother Quint Sellar
npcs.description: Keeps the chapel and the parish rolls; believes the Radiant counts honest tallies too.
npcs.physicalDescription: Grey-robed, ink-stained fingers

npcs.name: Ser Gavrel Thorn
npcs.description: Drills six soldiers and a boy, mostly against boredom; the walls have never been tested.
npcs.physicalDescription: Broad, greying soldier, whistle on a cord

npcs.name: Dara Wick
npcs.description: Takes the morning watch at the gate and knows every carter by their axle noise.
npcs.physicalDescription: Sun-browned soldier, shield scarred at the rim

npcs.name: Tom Wick
npcs.description: Weighs the toll-cart and counts it twice when his sister is watching.
npcs.physicalDescription: Lanky young man, rope-burned palms

npcs.name: Old Pew
npcs.description: Thirty years on the tower stairs; says the woodward's birds report to nobody.
npcs.physicalDescription: Wizened, wrapped in an old cloak

npcs.name: Sorrel Ash
npcs.description: Brenna's daughter: carries more jugs than her arms should allow and remembers every order.
npcs.physicalDescription: Quick-eyed girl, braids pinned with a brass pin

npcs.name: Gideon Marsh
npcs.description: Hauls the valley's grain and grudges with one mule named Treasurer.
npcs.physicalDescription: Thick-set man, cart grease on his cuffs

npcs.name: Petra Marsh
npcs.description: Keeps the village's coughs and confinements; trades yarrows with the farms.
npcs.physicalDescription: Calm woman, basket of drying herbs

npcs.name: Cobb Marsh
npcs.description: Pumps Ordwin's bellows and pockets the sparks he shouldn't.
npcs.physicalDescription: Soot-fringed boy, forever grinning

npcs.name: Widow Elnora Vane
npcs.description: Sews the garrison's coats and the village's opinions; grumbles at every toll rise.
npcs.physicalDescription: Straight-backed, spectacles on a ribbon

npcs.name: Silas Vane
npcs.description: Poles the ferry and sweeps the millrace; the river's only real friend.
npcs.physicalDescription: Barefoot boy, trousers rolled to the knee

npcs.name: Lomm Sage
npcs.description: Lodges at the Stag for a copper a week; the village's rats and rumours both reach him first.
npcs.physicalDescription: Lean man, ferret in a box

npcs.name: Reed Farren
npcs.description: Works Tilla's strips like they were his own; they nearly are.
npcs.physicalDescription: Weather-beaten man, straw behind one ear

npcs.name: Nan Osier
npcs.description: Turns the valley's milk into its butter, and the surplus into leverage.
npcs.physicalDescription: Sturdy girl, cheeks like apples

npcs.name: Tam Osier

npcs.physicalDescription: Gawky boy, switch in hand

npcs.name: Jorun Millrace

npcs.physicalDescription: Serious girl, chalk at her apron

npcs.name: Wat Underwood

npcs.physicalDescription: Quiet man, smelling of leaf-rot

frame.premise: A small castle on a rise above a farming village, counting its stores against a winter everyone feels coming.
frame.conflict: The count wants the granary full by first snow; the village wants the toll thinned
frame.playerRole: a traveler wintering at the Gilded Stag, handy with a quill
themes: a small place against a big winter
constraints: Keep it cozy: real danger stays beyond the walls
frame.summary: Ashvale is a small castle above a farming valley: four towers, a gatehouse, and a keep that has never been taken. The village of Emberwick clusters around its green, and the farms run their strips down to the river and the mill. Winter is coming early this year, and the count's castellan has begun counting everything twice - the granary, the toll, the sacks, the swords. The village counts back. The player is a traveler wintering at the Gilded Stag Inn, handy with a quill, slowly becoming the one both sides trust to keep an honest tally. It is a cozy world of suppers, markets, drills and small debts, where the only real danger is the cold and the river's old, honoured bargains.
unresolved: how early the winter truly comes
